READABILITY.evidence: The API types have clear names (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie, ConsistentHashRegexRewrite) and every field has a doc comment. Plugin code is split into named helpers (applyConsistentHash in consistent_hash.go). It follows the repo's existing comment style.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: The structure follows the plugin pattern: a separate consistent_hash.go, an IR, an apply step and merge wiring. Deepcopy and CRD came from `make go-generate-apis`. But consistent_hash.go runs past line 369 and mixes build, dedup, merge and apply in one file. It is unclear whether build and merge share the dedup helpers.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: The CRD has MinLength=1 on key fields and a CEL rule making disable exclusive. TTL parsing (duration or integer seconds) was implemented and tests pass. But Substitution is optional while Pattern is required, regex validity is not visibly checked at the API boundary, and the Terminal *bool pointers are used everywhere.

C7-09-CASE1.evidence: The golden /merged route shows the union with the higher-priority entries first. X-User-ID survives and x-user-id is dropped, so header dedup is case-insensitive. Order is headers → cookies → queryParameter → filterState. Metadata has `consistentHash: [route-level..., rule-level...]` under merge.TrafficPolicy.gateway.kgateway.dev. Hidden tests pass.

C7-09-CASE2.evidence: The CEL rule `!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers) && ...)` is on ConsistentHash and appears in the generated CRD. On the /disabled route, the rule-level disable removes the inherited hashPolicy. The empty-consistent-hash-policy test is in the golden file, and the hidden F2P tests pass.
